auq_a_voice_in_the_hall.description: I want the ground heard in the Council Hall, not just looked at. The houses have looked at the ground and the Earthborn for a hundred years and listened for about a week. I want that to change before the Ascendancy changes it for us. Go round to the Ground Embassy, a long walk south-east of here, and climb its steps. Tell Ambassador Tavia Morrane that the embassy speaks in the hall from now on, at every sitting.
auq_a_voice_in_the_hall.accept_text: She'll pretend she isn't surprised, so let her.

auq_built_for_guests.description: I took rubbings off the oldest hinge plates on the Spire's great doors, the ones the keepers have polished for a thousand years without reading. The script is ours, an old form of it. The measurements beside it aren't. Keeper of the Spire Ulmar Seyth won't listen to me, because my house is a joke to his. He might listen to you, so take him the rubbings.
auq_built_for_guests.accept_text: Don't tell him I sent them until he's looked. He'll read them honestly if he doesn't know.

auq_does_the_ground_have_scholars.description: The Academy's students keep asking whether the ground has scholars, and Halvric Oune keeps telling them nobody knows. The survey knows. I've got notes on the ground's libraries and colleges, and the Earthborn's universities too. Take them to the Master of the Academy. He won't enjoy being wrong in front of his faculty, so be kind about it.
auq_does_the_ground_have_scholars.accept_text: Give them to him privately if you can. He'll read them faster without an audience.

auq_fewer_every_year.description: I've watched the long-haulers dwindle for years. Look out from the Skydocks' rim first, and count the berths with nothing in them. Then go to the Anchorfields, because every Ascendancy Crystal-Weaver at the Second Anchor's camp is wearing crystal pulled out of a long-hauler's engine. I know, because I signed for some of it. Make them stop.
auq_fewer_every_year.accept_text: Count the empty berths properly. I want you to understand what they're taking.

auq_grafts_from_the_estate.description: Three of my oldest trees have stopped fruiting in my time, and the books don't tell me why. House Vaelith took cuttings from this orchard when they built their estate garden in the Anchorfields, centuries ago, and their trees are younger and stronger than mine now. Every Garden Repair-Drone on that estate carries sealed grafts in its kit, and they seal them properly, whatever else has gone wrong with them. Bring me clean wood. I'll graft it onto the trees that have stopped.
auq_grafts_from_the_estate.accept_text: Don't unseal them. The wood has to arrive the way the drones packed it.

auq_how_far_it_has_gone.description: The Ascendancy took the Second Anchor and told the wardens it was on the council's word. I never gave that word, and neither did any house. Every Ascendancy Warden at that camp carries written orders. I need to know whose seal is on them. Bring me enough of their orders that the houses can't call it one captain's mistake.
auq_how_far_it_has_gone.accept_text: The houses will want more than one. Bring me a handful.

auq_lenses_from_the_keel.description: The survey's lenses are cut from crystal that grows in the dark, and there's none darker than the crystal under the Third Anchor. Every Keel-Crystal Shard down in the Keel carries a lens inside it, already ground, if you break it cleanly. The other houses call my survey a waste of crystal. I'd like to show them otherwise. The Warden-Prime will let you in, because he owes you that much and more.
auq_lenses_from_the_keel.accept_text: Break them cleanly, along the grain. A cracked lens is just a pretty stone.

auq_letters_from_the_wards.description: I lived three years as one of the scholar houses' Earthborn wards. The wards still at Lenswatch gave me letters for the Ground Embassy, and some of them have been up here longer than me and never been allowed to write to anyone. Hamid Sadeghi at the embassy knows what to do with them. I want them in his hands today. Go now, please, before somebody on the council decides letters need a permit.
auq_letters_from_the_wards.accept_text: Don't stop on the way, and don't let anyone read them before Hamid does.

auq_soup_for_the_eighth.description: I feed everyone at the Eighth's Rest on the council's bread and the houses' coin. Bread and coin don't make a soup, wherever you're from, and meat does. The Eighth used to keep goats, on pasture on the outermost ring, and the herds went down with it. The Tiltside Goat out on the Anchorfields' Listing Isle is lean and stubborn, and it cooks down into something that'll keep an old man warm all night. Bring me shanks, and I'll feed the whole Rest on them.
auq_soup_for_the_eighth.accept_text: Good thick shanks. Half of them will cry when they taste it, and that's all right.

auq_the_doors_are_too_big.description: I sit for the House of Long Memory, and my house says the Spire Palace was built for somebody taller than an Aetherian. Everyone in Aurelion walks past the Spire every day and never looks at it. You haven't learned not to look yet. Go south to the Spire and stand at the great doors, then the winged column by the stair, then the guardian on the far side of the palace isle. Tell me what's wrong with all three, before the other houses tell you what to see.
auq_the_doors_are_too_big.accept_text: Look at them as if you'd never heard a word about them, because you haven't.

auq_the_free_skiffs.description: A few skiff captains still fly out to the Ascendant Bastions, to a wreck the Ascendancy can't reach. There's a camp there, in the wreck of a war-skiff called the Dawnspear, and the deserters send word of what the yard's building. The free skiffs fly to it from the end of my docks, past the airship dock on the rim. Take this letter to Captain Isolde Marrane, who runs the camp. She'll want to know the city's finally listening.
auq_the_free_skiffs.accept_text: Pay the captain before you board, not after. They leave faster that way.

auq_the_oldest_trees.description: Nobody understands Aurelion until they've walked the Gardens. My house is split down the middle, and the half that still speaks to me says I'm too fond of the ground, and they're welcome to think so. I'll show the ground the best thing we have. Walk west round the Inner Ring to the Gardens, see the great conservatory and the gold orchard, and find Gardener Tamsin Ashgrove. Don't pick an apple, because she counts them.
auq_the_oldest_trees.accept_text: Walk slowly through the orchard, because it was planted to be walked slowly.

auq_the_shortest_proclamation.description: I read the proclamation that opened Aurelion to the ground, and it was the shortest in the record. The council argued for a hundred years and then wrote eleven words, because nobody could bear to write any more. I've read nine hundred years of proclamations from this plaza, and none of them mattered more. Take my copy up past the Spire to the Council Hall, and give it to First Speaker Aldren Sorvaine. He'll want to see who it was for, and look you in the eye.
auq_the_shortest_proclamation.accept_text: Hand it to him yourself. Don't let a clerk take it at the door.

auq_up_the_grand_avenue.description: I've read the Warden-Prime's report, and it says the outer rings are safe because of you, and it's gone up to the council. The council wants to see the newcomer it's about. Walk straight north up the Grand Avenue from the gate, between the colossi, into the Grand Plaza. Stand by the light fountain, and Herald Odric Fane will find you. He's been waiting there since dawn.
auq_up_the_grand_avenue.accept_text: Don't stop to stare at the colossi. Everyone does, and the herald's patient, but not that patient.

auq_what_the_eighth_remembers.description: I watched the Eighth Ring fall. The memorial has every name we lost, and I'd like a guest from the ground to stand by it a while. Then walk out along the stub, north-west past the Rest, to where the ring breaks off. That's as close to home as any of us can get now. Come back and tell me what you saw out there.
auq_what_the_eighth_remembers.accept_text: Go to the very end. Don't stop short, the way most people do.

auq_where_everything_is.description: You're the city's first guest from the ground, and before the council gets hold of you, I want you to learn the Bridgefoot. You should know where to sleep, where to sell and where to catch a skiff before anything else happens. The Arro guesthouse is on the west side of the square, the Exchange is on the east, and the skiffs go from the dock past the guesthouse. Walk round all three. Then you won't be asking a guard for directions in front of the whole city.
auq_where_everything_is.accept_text: Take your time. The council can wait an hour, whatever they tell you.
